issues.explanation: Original omits the instruction to add capacitors for proper operation. Both extractions omit the illustrated connections: C1 between pins 1 and 3, C2 between pins 4 and 5, C3 from V+ to GND with VCC as an explicit alternative, C4 between V− and GND, and a 0.1 μF VCC bypass capacitor. Preserve the illustrated polarity when using polarized tantalum or electrolytic capacitors; nonpolarized ceramic capacitors are acceptable. These are application-section instructions, subject to TI's stated application-information qualification.
Both extractions omit the illustrated internal 5 kΩ pulls from RIN1 and RIN2 to ground. The figure states that resistor values are nominal.
Both extractions omit the explicit alternative that ROUT and DIN connect to general purpose logic lines as well as UART lines.

Application design conditions omit the recommended VCC of 3.3 V or 5 V, the permitted 3 V to 5.5 V range, and the maximum recommended bit rate of 250 kbit/s. The waveform caption alone does not preserve the bit-rate recommendation.
The connection extraction omits that V+ (pin 2) and V− (pin 6) are charge-pump outputs for storage capacitors only.
The driver input voltage limits omit the source qualification that all voltages are measured with respect to network GND.
The receiver input voltage limits omit the source qualification that all voltages are measured with respect to network GND.
The driver output voltage limits omit the source qualification that all voltages are measured with respect to network GND.
The receiver output voltage limits, including the symbolic maximum V_CC + 0.3 V, omit the source qualification that all voltages are measured with respect to network GND.

Original extraction omits receiver logic-output limits: VOH minimum VCC − 0.6 V, typical VCC − 0.1 V at IOH = −1 mA; VOL maximum 0.4 V at IOL = 1.6 mA. These apply over recommended supply and free-air-temperature ranges unless otherwise noted; typical values use VCC = 3.3 V or 5 V and TA = 25°C, with the specified capacitor test conditions. This is an original-reader coverage gap in the additional receiver source.

Original extraction omits receiver input thresholds: VIT+ typical/maximum = 1.5/2.4 V at VCC = 3.3 V and 1.8/2.4 V at 5 V; VIT− minimum/typical = 0.6/1.2 V at 3.3 V and 0.8/1.5 V at 5 V. Preserve recommended temperature ranges, TA = 25°C for typical values, and capacitor test conditions. This is an original-reader coverage gap in the additional receiver source.

The original omits power-pin assignments: VCC pin 16, GND pin 15, V+ pin 2, and V− pin 6. V+ and V− are respectively positive and negative charge-pump outputs for storage capacitors only; the independent extraction captures their uses but also omits their pin numbers.

Both extractions omit explicit capacitor wiring shown in Figure 9-1: the 0.1 μF bypass connects VCC pin 16 to GND; C1 connects C1+ pin 1 to C1− pin 3; C2 connects C2+ pin 4 to C2− pin 5; C3 connects V+ pin 2 to GND, with VCC as the stated alternative; C4 connects V− pin 6 to GND. For polarized capacitors, the diagram shows positive terminals at C1+, C2+, V+ for C3, and GND for C4.
Both extractions omit Figure 9-1 footnote †: C3 can be connected to VCC or GND.
The layout example also shows C1 connected between C1+ (pin 1) and C1− (pin 3), and C2 between C2+ (pin 4) and C2− (pin 5). These illustrated capacitor connections are omitted.

The illustrated ground connections are not extracted: C3 connects V+ (pin 2) to ground, C4 connects V− (pin 6) to ground, the 0.1-µF capacitor connects VCC (pin 16) to ground, and GND (pin 15) connects to ground. These are layout-example connections; they do not establish ground-plane, return-path-routing or thermal-via requirements.

The image shows the merged CL = 150 pF condition spanning only the two propagation-delay rows. The receiver pulse-skew row has a separate blank condition cell; assigning CL = 150 pF to it is unsupported. The independent extraction correctly omits that condition.

Both extractions omit Figure 7-1's device transition-time definition: SR(tr) = 6 V / tTHL or 6 V / tTLH, measured between output +3 V and −3 V. These are transition-region times, not a separate full-output rise/fall-time specification.

Both extractions omit measurement conditions supplied by Figures 7-1 and 7-2: CL includes probe and jig capacitance; the generator has PRR = 250 kbit/s, ZO = 50 Ω, 50% duty cycle, tr ≤ 10 ns and tf ≤ 10 ns. Driver input waveforms span 0–3 V with 1.5 V timing references; pulse-skew delays use output 50% crossings. Generator tr/tf limits are not device rise/fall limits.

Both extractions leave the propagation-delay target unspecified. Figure 7-3 identifies these as receiver propagation delays and supplies output 50% timing references, a −3 V to +3 V input waveform, CL including probe and jig capacitance, and generator conditions ZO = 50 Ω, 50% duty cycle, tr ≤ 10 ns and tf ≤ 10 ns.
Driver pulse skew 300 ns is in the TYP column, not MAX. Preserve RL = 3–7 kΩ, CL = 150–2500 pF, Figure 7-2, and common switching conditions; typical values apply at VCC = 3.3 V or 5 V and TA = 25°C.

Additional source coverage supplies a maximum recommended bit rate of 250 kbit/s, absent from the original. This application recommendation is distinct from the switching table's 150 kbit/s minimum and 250 kbit/s typical maximum-data-rate values. Preserve the qualification that application information is outside TI's component specification, is not warranted for accuracy or completeness, and requires customer suitability assessment and design validation/testing.
The original mentions capacitor-trace guidance but omits its actionable content: keep external capacitor traces short, especially C1 and C2 nodes, which have the fastest rise and fall times.
Receiver pulse skew also has C_L = 150 pF: the merged test-condition cell spans both receiver propagation-delay rows and the receiver pulse-skew row. The original omits this load condition.
Both extractions omit the Figure 9-1 dagger note: C3 can be connected to VCC or GND.

The original omits package-option footnote (2), retained by the independent extraction. When designated, preproduction parts are prototypes/experimental devices not approved or released for full production; testing and qualification may be incomplete, changes or discontinuation remain possible, and ordering requires an additional checkout waiver for early internal evaluation, without warranties. This conditional definition does not establish that MAX3232CD is preproduction.

Both extractions omit the qualified-version definition: Enhanced Product supports Defense, Aerospace and Medical Applications. Preserve its scope as a version definition; the supplied evidence does not designate MAX3232CD as Enhanced Product.

The original omits the measurement test-circuit loads: Figures 7-1 and 7-2 show a 50 Ω generator termination and output loads RL and CL to ground; Figure 7-3 shows a 50 Ω generator termination and output capacitance CL to ground. RL and CL are symbolic; no numerical load values are specified.

8 Detailed Description
8.1 Overview
The MAX3232 device consists of two line drivers, two line receivers, and a dual charge-pump circuit with ±15-kV
ESD protection terminal to terminal (serial-port connection terminals, including GND). The device meets the
requirements of TIA/EIA-232-F and provides the electrical interface between an asynchronous communication
controller and the serial-port connector. The charge pump and four small external capacitors allow operation
from a single 3-V to 5.5-V supply. The device operates at data signaling rates up to 250 kbit/s and a maximum of
30-V/μs driver output slew rate. Outputs are protected against shorts to ground.
